vulnerability_analysis: The Escrow contract has a re-entrancy vulnerability in the withdraw function. The function calls IWETH(WETH).withdraw(_amount) which sends ETH to the contract, then updates the balance (_balances[sender] = _balances[sender].sub(_amount)), and finally transfers ETH to _to using TransferHelper.safeTransferETH(_to, _amount). If _to is a malicious contract with a receive() or fallback() function, it can re-enter the withdraw function before the balance is updated, allowing multiple withdrawals with the same balance check.
attack_strategy: 1. Set up the attacker as both owner and spender. 2. Deposit some ETH to get a balance. 3. Create a malicious contract that re-enters the withdraw function. 4. Call withdraw to the malicious contract, which will re-enter multiple times, draining more funds than the initial balance.
step_by_step_plan: 1. In setUp(), get some ETH using deal(). 2. Call setSpender on the target contract to set attacker as spender. 3. Call deposit with some ETH to get a balance. 4. Deploy a malicious contract with a re-entrant receive() function. 5. Call withdraw to the malicious contract address with an amount. 6. The malicious contract's receive() will be called with ETH, and it will re-enter withdraw again. 7. Repeat until contract balance is drained or gas runs out.
